description_full: Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, owns and operates utility investments in Brazil, the United Kingdom, and internationally. It also engages in the regulated gas and electricity business; and operation of regulated natural gas transmission systems. The company operates approximately 2,000 kilometers of natural gas transportation pipelines in the states of Rio de Janeiro, Sao Paulo, and Minas Gerais, Brazil; gas and electricity connections in the United Kingdom; and a global fleet of twenty-foot equivalent units intermodal containers under long-term contracts. The company was incorporated in 2019 and is headquartered in New York, New York. Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation operates as a subsidiary of Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P.

financial_summary: Brookfield Infrastructure Corpo is a mid-cap utilities business with a $4.9B market cap on $3.7B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +25% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

The business throws off $2M in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.30× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.0× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 4.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.2× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
